# AF 第五章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 5

[P01] As winter came, Mollie became more troublesome（麻烦的）. She was late every morning and said she overslept（睡过头）. She complained of pains, but ate well. She often ran away to the drinking pool and stood looking at her reflection（反思）. There were also rumours（谣言） of something worse. One day, Mollie walked into the yard, moving her tail and chewing（咀嚼） hay（干草）. Clover took her aside（旁边）. "Mollie," she said, "I have something very serious to say to you.

[P02] "This morning I saw you by the hedge（树篱） between Animal Farm and Foxwood（狐林）. One of Mr. Pilkington's men stood on the other side. I was far away, but I am almost sure he talked to you, and you let him touch your nose. What does that mean, Mollie?"

"He didn't（没有）! I wasn't（不是）! It isn't（不是） true!" cried Mollie. She jumped about and hit the ground with her foot.

"Mollie! Look at me. Do you promise, on your honour, that the man did not touch your nose?"

"It isn't true!" Mollie said again, but she could not look at Clover. Then she ran away fast into the field. A thought came to Clover.

[P03] She said nothing. She went to Mollie's stall（畜栏） and turned over the straw（稻草） with her hoof（蹄） without saying anything to the others. She found lump（块） sugar and coloured ribbons（丝带） under it. This made Clover think.

Three days later Mollie was gone. For some weeks no one knew where she was. Then the pigeons saw her in Willingdon. She was between the poles（杆子） of a red and black dogcart（狗车） outside a pub（酒吧）. A fat man with a red face was stroking her nose and giving her sugar.

[P04] Her coat was new and she had a red ribbon（丝带） on her head. The pigeons said she looked happy. No animal talked about Mollie again.

In January the weather became very cold. The earth was like iron. No work could be done in the fields. Many meetings were held in the big barn（谷仓）. The pigs planned the work for the next season. It was accepted that the pigs were cleverer than the others, so they decided all farm questions, but a majority（大多数） vote had to agree.

[P05] This plan worked, but Snowball and Napoleon often argued. They disagreed（不同意） at every point. If one wanted more barley（大麦）, the other wanted more oats（燕麦）. If one said a field was good for cabbages, the other said it was good for nothing but roots. Each had his own followers（追随者）, and there were wild debates. At the Meetings Snowball often won the majority with his brilliant（聪明的） speeches, but Napoleon was better at getting support in between.

[P06] He was very good with the sheep. Lately the sheep had started bleating"Four legs good, two legs bad" all the time, and they often stopped the Meeting with it. Snowball had studied old papers from the farmhouse（农舍）, and had many plans for new ideas. He talked in a learned way about field drains（排水沟） and silage（青贮饲料）, and had made a plan for all the animals to drop their dung（粪便） in the fields, at a different spot（地点） every day, to save the labour（劳作） of cartage（运货）.

[P07] Napoleon had no schemes（计划） of his own, but he said quietly that Snowball's schemes would come to nothing, and he seemed to be waiting for his time. But of all their fights, none was so angry as the one about the windmill（风车）. These two disagreed on every point where they could disagree（不同意）. In the long pasture（牧场）, not far from the farm buildings, there was a small hill. It was the highest point on the farm.

[P08] After looking at the ground, Snowball said this was the right place for a windmill. It could make electricity. This would light the stalls（畜栏） and keep them warm in winter. It would also run machines to cut wood, cut grass, cut food, and milk the cows. The animals had never heard of such things. Their farm was old and had only simple machines. Snowball showed them machines that would do their work. Then the animals could eat grass or read and talk. In a few weeks, Snowball finished his plans for the windmill.

[P09] The mechanical（机械的） details came mostly from three books that had belonged to Mr. Jones. Snowball used an old shed for his study. Its smooth wooden floor was good for drawing. He stayed in there for hours. He held his books open with a stone（石头） and gripped（攫住） a piece of chalk between his trotter（猪蹄） knuckles（指关节）. He moved quickly back and forth（向前）, drawing line after line. Slowly the plans grew into a complex（复杂的） mass（大量） of cranks（曲柄） and cog（齿轮）-wheels. The other animals found it impossible to understand, but very impressive（令人印象深刻）.

[P10] All the animals came to see Snowball's drawings. Even the hens and ducks came and tried not to step on the chalk marks. Only Napoleon stayed away. He had said no to the windmill from the start. One day, he came to look at the plans. He walked heavily（沉重地） round the shed, looked closely at every detail, and snuffed（嗅） at them. Then he stood for a while, looking at them from the corner of his eye. Then he suddenly lifted his leg and urinated（撒尿） over the plans, and walked out without a word. The whole farm was deeply divided about the windmill.

[P11] Snowball did not denythat building it would be hard. Stone must be carried to make walls. Then sails, dynamos（发电机） and cables（电缆） were needed. Snowball did not say how to get these. But he said it could be done in a year. Then the animals would only work three days a week. Napoleon argued that they needed more food now. If they wasted time on the windmill, they would all starve（饿死） to death.

[P12] The animals split（分裂） into two groups. One group said, "Vote for Snowball and a three-day week." The other said, "Vote for Napoleon and a full manger（食槽）." Benjamin did not join either side. He did not believe that food would become more plentiful（丰富） or that the windmill would save work. Windmill or no windmill, he said, life would go on as before—that is, badly. Besides the windmill, there was the question of defending（保卫） the farm. The humans had lost the Battle of the Cowshed（牛棚）, but they might try again to take back the farm and put Mr. Jones back.

[P13] Jones. They had more reason because news of their defeat spread. This made animals on nearby farms more restless（不安）. Snowball and Napoleon did not agree. According to Napoleon, the animals must get guns and train to use them. According to Snowball, they must send out more pigeons to start uprisings on other farms. One said if they could not defend（保卫） themselves, they would be beaten. The other said if rebellions (叛乱) happened in 1 place everywhere, they would not need to defend themselves.

[P14] The animals listened to Napoleon first, then to Snowball. They could not decide who was right. In fact, they always agreed with the one who was speaking at that moment. At last Snowball finished his plans. On Sunday, at the Meeting, they would vote on whether to start work on the windmill. When the animals came together in the big barn, Snowball stood up. The sheep bleated sometimes, but he gave his reasons for building the windmill.

[P15] Then Napoleon stood up. He said quietly that the windmill was nonsense（胡说） and no one should vote for it. Then he sat down. He had spoken for only thirty seconds. Snowball jumped up. The sheep had begun bleating again, and he shouted them down. He then made a passionate（热情的） speech for the windmill. The animals had been divided, but Snowball's words carried them away. He painted a picture of Animal Farm with no hard labour.

[P16] His imagination went far beyond farm tools. Electricity, he said, could run threshing（打谷） machines, ploughs, harrows（耙）, rollers（滚筒）, reapers（收割机） and binders（捆扎机）. It could also give every stall its own electric light, hot and cold water, and an electric heater. When he finished, everyone knew how the vote would go. But then Napoleon stood up. He gave Snowball a strange sidelong（斜眼） look and made a high-pitched（投掷） whimper（呜咽）—a sound no one had heard from him before. Then, a terrible baying（吠叫） sound came from outside. Nine huge dogs with brass（黄铜）-studded（镶嵌） collars（项圈） ran into the barn.

[P17] They ran straight at Snowball. He jumped away just in time. In a moment he was out of the door, and the dogs ran after him. All the animals were too surprised and afraid to speak. They ran out to watch. Snowball ran across the long field to the road. He ran as fast as a pig can run, but the dogs were right behind him. Suddenly he slipped（滑倒）, and it looked like they had caught him. Then he was up again, running even faster. One dog almost bit his tail, but Snowball pulled it away just in time.

[P18] Then he ran faster. He got through a hole in the hedge, and then no one saw him again. He ran fast, but the dogs were right behind him. The animals were silent and very afraid. They crept（爬行） back into the barn. Soon the dogs came bounding（跳跃） back. At first no one knew where these animals came from, but the answer came soon: they were the puppies Napoleon had taken from their mothers and raised by himself.

[P19] The dogs were not fully grown, but they were huge and fierce like wolves. They stayed close to Napoleon. They wagged（摇摆） their tails at him, just as they once did to Mr. Jones. Napoleon climbed onto the raised part of the floor where Major had stood before. The dogs followed him. He said the Sunday-morning Meetings would end. They wasted time, he said. From now on, a special committee（委员会） of pigs, led by himself, would decide all questions about the farm.

[P20] The pigs met alone and then told the others what they decided. The animals still met on Sunday mornings to salute（敬礼） the flag, sing 'Beasts（野兽） of England', and get orders for the week. But there was no more talking. The animals were shocked and afraid by Snowball's expulsion（驱逐）. Some wanted to protest（抗议） but found no words. Even Boxer was worried. He put his ears back, shook his mane（鬃毛）, and tried to think. But he found nothing to say.

[P21] But some pigs could speak better. Four young pigs in the front row cried out in disagreement（分歧）. They all stood up and began to speak at once. Then the dogs around Napoleon gave deep, angry growls（咆哮）. The pigs stopped and sat down again. Then the sheep began a great bleating of "Four legs good, two legs bad!" It lasted almost a quarter of an hour and stopped any talk. Later Squealer was sent around the farm to explain the new plan. "Comrades（同志们）," he said, "I believe every animal here sees the sacrifice（牺牲） that Comrade（同志） Napoleon has made by taking this extra（额外） hard work on himself.

[P22] Do not think, comrades, that leadership（领导） is fun! No, it is a big and heavy job. No one believes more than Comrade Napoleon that all animals are equal. He would be happy to let you decide things. But sometimes you might decide wrong, and then what would happen? What if you had followed Snowball, with his silly windmills（风车）? Snowball was just a criminal（罪犯）! "He fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed," said somebody. "Bravery（勇敢） is not enough," said Squealer. "Loyalty（忠诚） and obedience（服从） matter more. And about the Battle of the Cowshed, I think the time will come when we find that Snowball's part in it was much bigger than it really was.

[P23] Discipline（纪律）, comrades, iron discipline! That is the word for today. One wrong step, and our enemies will come. Surely, comrades, you do not want Jones back? The animals did not want Jones back. If talking could bring him back, then the talking must stop. Boxer had time to think. He said what all felt: "If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right." He took the saying, "Napoleon is always right," and his own, "I will work harder." Spring ploughing had begun.

[P24] The shed where Snowball drew his windmill plans was closed. People thought the plans were rubbed off the floor. Every Sunday at ten, the animals met in the big barn for orders. Old Major's skull（头骨） was dug up and put on a stump（树桩） near the flagstaff（旗杆） and the gun. After the flag went up, the animals walked past the skull quietly before going into the barn.

[P25] Napoleon sat at the front of the platform（舞台） with Squealer and another pig, Minimus, who was good at writing songs and poems. The nine young dogs sat in a half-circle around them, and the other pigs sat behind. The rest of the animals sat facing them in the barn. Napoleon read the week's orders in a rough, soldier-like way. After they sang 'Beasts of England' once, all the animals went away. The weather had turned bad. On the third Sunday after Snowball was driven out, the animals were surprised to hear Napoleon say that the windmill would be built after all.

[P26] He did not say why he had changed his mind. He only told the animals that the extra work would be very hard, and they might have to eat less. But the plans were ready. A group of pigs had worked on them for three weeks. The windmill would take two years to build. That evening Squealer told the animals that Napoleon had never been against the windmill. He had wanted it from the start, and Snowball's plan had really been stolen from Napoleon's papers.

[P27] The windmill was, in fact, Napoleon's own idea. Why, then, had he spoken so strongly against it? Here Squealer looked very sly（狡猾的）. That, he said, was Comrade Napoleon's clever plan. He had seemed to be against the windmill, just to get rid of Snowball, a dangerous character. Now that Snowball was gone, the plan could go on. This, said Squealer, was called tactics（策略）. He said many times, "Tactics, comrades, tactics!" jumping round with a merry（快乐） laugh. The animals were not sure what the word meant, but Squealer spoke so well, and the three dogs growled（咆哮） so threateningly（威胁地）, that they accepted his explanation without more questions.
